blocks.x: Herd health on IoT evidence — clinical mastitis detected days earlier, milk yield up 5% and antibiotic use down 18%
a dairy group whose herd health depended on the 4:30 a.m. observation skills of whoever was milking. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter counted the observations missed: clinical mastitis diagnosed at visible symptoms rather than onset, 2.1% milk yield loss to subclinical infection, and antibiotic use that neither the co-op's premiums nor the regulators wanted at that level.
Sensor data existed on half the farms but lived in vendor apps nobody read. The vet saw the herd after the farmer saw the cow after the yield had already dropped.

We built the herd twin: sensor streams — yield, conductivity, activity — normalized across farms into one health model, anomaly signatures learned per breed and lactation stage with vets labeling confirmed cases, early-warning alerts routed to farm and vet with the evidence attached, and treatment outcomes feeding the signatures back. The 4:30 a.m. instincts became a model that works all day.
